blogTitle: The Gina Files: Paranormal Case Notes (Sources Cited)
about: ok so. i'm gina, i'm 16, and i'm the founder, sole investigator and treasurer of the Ohio Valley Paranormal Society, Junior Division (membership: 1. my brother Danny doesn't count, he says he's 'observing'). i own a digital voice recorder, a flashlight with a red filter, a kitchen thermometer (for cold spots), a spiral notebook (numbered, dated), and a stud finder that is also a 'presence detector' (mr h says it's a stud finder). my current case is the school auditorium. i have 14 hours of audio. 11 hours are the fridge. i know it's the fridge. that's called a control. the other 3 hours are Under Review. i'm not here to scare anybody. i'm here to listen.
aboutMore: rules for my page: 1) all sightings welcome, including 'it was probably the wind.' i want the wind in the file. 2) i don't believe everything. i believe in writing everything down. 3) orbs are mostly dust and moisture (mr h explained backscatter, i made a chart). i have 400 orb photos anyway. they're pretty and i'm keeping them. 4) if you hear your name in an empty room, say 'thank you' and keep walking. it's polite and nothing has ever gone wrong.
meet: Who i'd like to meet: whoever says 'again from the top' in the balcony at 4:44 PM (hi. i'm not mad. i have cocoa). Ms. Marchetti's cat, who attended 5 of my 7 sessions and never once looked at the corner. the pipe guys from the ghost show on TV, to ask what the 'shadow' was (it's a coat). and anyone who has ever heard the house make a noise and said 'hello?' out loud. you're my people.

interests.General: EVP (electronic voice phenomena), cold-spot mapping, orb photography (400 and counting), the school auditorium after 3:15 (with a hall pass), the ghost light (it's definitely for the ghosts), spiral notebooks, checking whether a sound is the fridge, cocoa in a thermos (investigating is cold), Mr. Henderson's extra credit
interests.Music: the hum of the walk-in cooler at the grocery store (very consistent), my brother's band practice (loud, not haunted), Evanescence (Fallen, front to back), My Chemical Romance, whatever my mom plays at 6 PM while she's getting ready for her shift. my profile song is the Rockwell one. i know. it's so obvious. my mom has it on cassette so now it's also 'family history'
interests.Movies: Ghostbusters (a documentary), The Haunting (the black and white one, the breathing door, seen it 9 times), Poltergeist (through my fingers), The Others, Scooby-Doo (the original cartoons. don't talk to me about the live action)
interests.Television: Ghost Hunters (i have the episode where they find a 'shadow.' it's a coat), Unsolved Mysteries, Buffy (the Halloween episode), the Twilight Zone marathon on New Year's Day, MythBusters (sources cited, i respect that)
interests.Books: Hans Holzer (library copy, overdue, renewed 4 times), The Haunting of Hill House (best book about methodology that is also fiction), Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark (sleeping with the light on, no regrets), my own notebooks #1 through #22
interests.Heroes: Houdini (spent years debunking mediums, looked at every trick and said 'show me,' and also wanted so badly for one to be real that he made a promise to his wife about it. both of those can be true at once). Mr. Henderson (3 points). Bill from the Bigfoot page, who heard my audio and said 'good control.' my mom, who is also awake at 3 AM

keywords.ghost: i don't say 'ghost.' i say 'unexplained auditory event.' it's more accurate and my notebook has more room. ...ok i say ghost when i'm tired.
keywords.orb: an orb in a flash photo is almost always dust, pollen or moisture caught in the flash (backscatter). i know. i have 400. i keep them anyway. technically they're a record of how much dust is in my room, which is also kind of beautiful.
keywords.fridge: it's the fridge. it's always the fridge. a refrigerator cycles on every 20 to 40 minutes and makes a note like a sleeping cello. i call it the control. everything else gets compared to it. i say thank you to it at the end of every session.
keywords.auditorium: case #14. a voice in the balcony says 'again from the top.' 9 seconds, 4:44 PM. thad says it's Ms. Marchetti. Ms. Marchetti was at home. i have the timestamp. either it's a ghost or the building has heard that line so many times it learned it. which is called a residual haunting. so it's a ghost either way.
keywords.evp: electronic voice phenomena: you record in an empty room, ask a question, leave a pause, then play it back. 90 percent of the time it's nothing. 9 percent it's a fridge. 1 percent is Under Review. that last 1 percent is why i own a thermos.
keywords.haunted: all houses are a little haunted. they make noise, they hold temperature, they remember how people walked through them. i'm just the one who writes it down.
keywords.bigfoot: bill's department. we have a cooperative agreement. he sends me 'control stump' updates. i send him fridge results.

blog.title: CASE FILE #14: The Voice In The Balcony (Sessions 4-7)
blog.body: CASE FILE #14. Location: school auditorium, balcony row B. Equipment: recorder, red flashlight, thermometer, one (1) stud finder (see Mr. H). Session 6, Friday, 4:44 PM: a voice, 9 seconds, clear, says 'again from the top.' Session 7, Friday, 4:31 PM: same voice, same line, 6 seconds. Ruled out: ventilation (Mr. H), the vending machine (Tim, ledger), my brother (karate). Ms. Marchetti was at home for both (timestamped photo of her empty parking space). Thad says the room has 'absorbed' her, since she says that line 40 times a day. I told him that's called a residual haunting and he said, 'Gina, I'm a theater kid, we invented being haunted by rooms.' Hypothesis: a building can hold a phrase the way a bell holds a note. Verdict: inconclusive (spooky). Next steps: session 8, cocoa, tenth row, and the ghost light, which I will not touch. Thank you to the auditorium for its time.

blog.title: CASE FILE #12: Why It's Always The Fridge (A Note On Controls)
blog.body: CASE FILE #12. Methodology. People ask why I keep recording my kitchen when I already know it's the fridge. Here's why. A control is the thing you compare everything else to. Without it you can't say what a ghost isn't. I recorded the kitchen for eight nights. Results: eight nights of fridge, one night of dishwasher, and one night of my mom humming at 3:10 AM when she got home from her shift, which I did not expect and have kept. Mr. H says a good scientist is happiest when the control behaves, because then the weird stuff is actually weird. I think about that a lot. Also, the hum is the sound of the house being okay. I fall asleep to it. At the end of every session I say thank you to the fridge. I don't know why. In case. Verdict: fridge. Always fridge. Beautifully, reliably fridge.

blog.title: CASE FILE #6: Orbs Are Dust (A Retraction I Am Not Retracting)
blog.body: CASE FILE #6. For two years I believed orbs were spirits. In May I took 400 flash photos at the old cemetery gate and every one had at least 2 orbs. Mr. Henderson looked at the best one and said, kindly, 'that's dust, Gina.' He explained backscatter: the flash lights up a speck close to the lens and it looks like a glowing disc. I was upset for a day. Then I made a chart of orbs per photo against humidity. It came out at 0.7, which he said is a real correlation and 'the best chart in the class.' So I am retracting my claim that orbs are ghosts. I am not retracting how they look. 400 little lights hanging in the dark, each one a speck of the actual air. That's pretty even if it's physics. Maybe especially. Verdict: dust. Gorgeous dust. Case closed. (File kept open for moths.)
